rationale: The adapter, file identities, memory controls, and descriptive replication are already validated. Broad Track-B execution would not resolve physical weighting or convert the evidence into efficiency, yield, AUC, or significance claims. Track A is the primary physics and native-model comparison lane.

This would broaden unweighted released-model response coverage across 18 groups, but it would not unlock physical interpretation. Its main value is descriptive external-dataset characterization, which is lower priority than Track-A normalization and native SPA-Net/ParT/JP-JEPA comparisons.

This would characterize rare high-response tails, but without physical weights, independent labels, or calibrated acceptance criteria it cannot support a physical contamination or sensitivity claim. A smaller targeted tail design may be revisited later.
